hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis or treatment goes wrong at a clinic or hospital serving Escalon families, MICRA's strict clocks start ticking fast. Our team can review your case at no cost and explain your options under California medical malpractice law.

about.title: Escalon Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Escalon is a small San Joaquin County community, and many residents travel to nearby Modesto or Stockton facilities for specialty care or surgery. That distance can complicate follow-up, records requests, and communication when something goes wrong during treatment. If a delayed diagnosis, surgical error, medication mistake, or birth injury left you or a family member worse off, California's MICRA law governs your options — including a one-year discovery deadline, a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider, and a mandatory qualified medical expert to establish that care fell below the accepted standard. A bad result by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the law requires showing the provider's conduct fell short of what a reasonably careful practitioner would have done. Our team handles medical malpractice claims and can help Escalon residents evaluate your case under California's medical malpractice framework.
commonInjuries: Birth injuries to mother or child

items.title: MICRA's Clock Moves Quickly
items.desc: California generally gives one year from discovery of the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim — we can help track which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires sending the provider a 90-day pre-suit notice; missing this step can delay or jeopardize a claim, so early attorney guidance matters.

items.title: Expert Testimony Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone doesn't establish malpractice, a qualified medical expert typically must confirm the care fell below the accepted standard — something our team knows how to arrange.

items.question: I live in Escalon but was treated in Modesto or Stockton — does that change my claim?
items.answer: No, California's MICRA rules apply based on where the care was provided, not where you live. We can review records from any facility in the region and explain how the notice and filing deadlines apply to your specific case.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date of the injury itself, with limited exceptions. These deadlines are strict, so it's wise to have a claim reviewed as soon as possible after suspecting an error.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, MICRA sets a statutory cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages like medical bills and lost income are generally not subject to this cap, and we can walk through how this applies to your circumstances.
